name: Jael
bio:
Jael was the wife of Heber the Kenite. When the Canaanite commander Sisera fled from his defeated army, he came to Jael's tent; she went out to meet him, saying, "Come, my lord, come right in. Don't be afraid," and gave him milk to drink instead of water, covering him so he could rest undisturbed (Judges 4:17-19).

Sisera asked her to lie on his behalf if anyone came searching for him, then fell into an exhausted sleep. While he slept, Jael took a tent peg and a hammer, crept up quietly, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground, killing him instantly (Judges 4:20-21). When Barak arrived in pursuit of Sisera, Jael came out to meet him and showed him Sisera lying dead with the tent peg through his temple (Judges 4:22).

In the victory song of Judges 5, Deborah and Barak singled out Jael for praise: "Most blessed of women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, most blessed of tent-dwelling women" (Judges 5:24), tying her courageous act directly to Israel's triumph and making her one of Scripture's clearest examples of a woman turning the tide of battle through resourcefulness and nerve.
